description: France's largest independent wealth-management/CGPI group, combining private wealth management, asset management and family office services. Formed April 2024 by the merger of Cyrus Conseil and Maison Herez, present in four major French cities plus Brussels and Tel Aviv. Owns AMF-approved asset-management subsidiaries Amplegest (GP-07000044, EUR 5.2bn) and Eternam (real estate, EUR 1.4bn) - see separate CRM records. Executive committee: Meyer Azogui (Group President), Patrick Ganansia (Group Vice-President), David Intins (CEO, Cyrus Herez).

fit.reasoning: Fit 55/60: priority segment family office/MFO (20) + priority market France (15) + multi-asset across its subsidiaries' equity/bond/real-estate/private-management offering (10) + third-party client money by definition of wealth/family-office management (10) + regulated indirectly through AMF-approved subsidiaries rather than a single group-level licence, so a partial 5 rather than full confidence. Trigger 12/25: the April 2024 Cyrus Conseil/Maison Herez merger is a genuine consolidation event - two wealth-management platforms combining almost certainly means reconciling client reporting and possibly back-office systems across the merged entity and its subsidiaries - but it does not map cleanly onto a single table row (closest: new entity from a merger, similar in spirit to a spin-out) and is now roughly 18 months old, so scored below the 20-point new-entity band. Access 8/15: named CEO David Intins and Group President Meyer Azogui identified via multiple press sources, not yet confirmed reachable. Total 75, moderated to 62: this is a large, already-sophisticated group (likely running established systems across its subsidiaries already) rather than a firm professionalising for the first time - qualify what, if anything, is actually still fragmented post-merger before assuming a live systems-review trigger. Coordinate with the Amplegest and Eternam records rather than pursuing all three independently.
